label: mid/late original-phase steps (t=3-7) after 0/y/q/b/l has been seen
explanation: Fires almost only during the original-token phase (97% of mass), at positions t=3-7 and peaking at t=4-6. It never fires at t=0-1, barely fires on <DEL> (3% of mass), and is essentially silent for the whole copy phase. Inside that window, how likely it is to fire depends on which tokens came earlier: the rate is highest when 0, y, q, b, l (and to a lesser degree g, 1, s, p) appear among the previous inputs, especially one or two steps back (prev2_tok=0 gives 4.1x lift). It is also more likely on the first occurrence of the current input (in_first) and in sequences with more digits. The strongest activations sit on runs of consecutive steps 1-3 positions after such a token (e.g. p l p y [0 w e 0]). The position window plus the seen-token condition captures about 90% of activation mass but only ~30% precision. Which steps fire inside the window seems to be a distributed function of prefix content that no simple predicate captured (best F1 ~0.48).
